draft.title: How diseases spread
card: Direct contact
a pathogen passes from an infected host to another host by touch, body fluids or a bite. Examples are skin contact and sexual contact.
Droplets
an infected person coughs, sneezes or talks and releases tiny drops of fluid that carry the pathogen. Another person breathes them in or they land on the eyes, nose or mouth.
Contaminated food or water
a pathogen gets into food or drinking water, often from faeces or poor handling. People who eat or drink it can become infected.
Vector
an organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another, usually without being harmed itself. A mosquito that carries malaria parasites is a vector.
draft.remember: Pathogens spread by contact, droplets, contaminated food or water, or a vector that carries them between hosts.

opts: An animal that carries a pathogen between hosts
A person who has caught a disease
A drop of fluid released by a sneeze
Food that has been contaminated by a pathogen
a.why: A vector is an organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another. A sneeze droplet and contaminated food carry a pathogen too, but they are not organisms that move it between hosts, so they are not vectors.
a.clue: A vector is a living thing that moves the pathogen.

b.q: Many people at a camp in Queensland get sick with diarrhoea after drinking from a creek that cattle had polluted with faeces. Which way did the disease spread?
opts: Contaminated water
Droplets
Vector
Direct contact
b.why: The pathogen reached people through water that faeces had contaminated. Direct contact is tempting because people were in the same place, but the pathogen was not passed by touching an infected person. No animal carried it from host to host, so it is not a vector.
b.clue: Think about what the people swallowed.

a.best: An animal that carries a pathogen between hosts

problems.detail: Direct contact lists 'a bite' as a route, while the vector example is a mosquito, which also spreads malaria by biting. Without saying it means a bite from an infected host, such as a dog with rabies, students may think a mosquito bite counts as direct contact.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. One small issue: the card lists 'a bite' under direct contact without separating it from a mosquito bite, which is the vector route.

Vector
